findings.title: Team admins are rejected by an AND between admin and owner checks
findings.description: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` matches ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284), but `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER (lines 286-295). The AND therefore lets only OWNER through, so ADMIN members of the event's team get FORBIDDEN. The variable name says the intent is admin-or-owner. Use `||`, or drop `isTeamOwner` since `isTeamAdmin` already includes OWNER.

findings.title: Blacklist is bypassed by upper-case letters and plus-addressing
findings.description: The env list is lowercased (line 71), but each guest is compared raw (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, line 77). `Blocked@Example.com` passes when the list contains `blocked@example.com`. `blocked+x@example.com` passes when the list contains `blocked@example.com`, because no base-address extraction happens here. The booking path normalizes both: handleNewBooking.ts:742-743 uses `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()`, and checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts:12-18 does the same. Apply the same normalization on the guest side.

findings.title: Calendar update failures are swallowed and the handler reports success
findings.description: Attendees are written to the DB at line 92, before the calendar update at line 165. `updateCalendarAttendees` returns `void` (packages/core/EventManager.ts:596-602), which discards the result of `updateAllCalendarEvents`. That function catches its own errors and returns `success: false` entries (EventManager.ts:921-939). The early return at lines 597-600 only calls `console.error`. The handler then returns "Guests added" (line 173) even when no invitation went out. editLocation.handler.ts:107-116 checks the calendar results and skips the DB write when every update fails. Mirror that, or surface partial failure to the caller.

findings.title: Email send failure is caught, logged without the error, and discarded
findings.description: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` drops `err`, so the cause can't be diagnosed. editLocation.handler.ts:5 and :114 use `@calcom/lib/logger` with the error object. Log `err` the same way.

findings.title: Server accepts duplicate and case-variant guests, creating duplicate attendee rows
findings.description: The server schema is `z.array(z.string().email())`, with no uniqueness check. The only uniqueness check is the dialog's Zod refine (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29). The handler filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) excludes only emails already on the booking, and it compares case-sensitively with `guest === attendee.email`. It does not dedupe within `guests`. The Attendee model has no unique constraint on `(bookingId, email)` (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:526-539). A direct call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` or `["A@x.com","a@x.com"]` therefore creates duplicate rows and duplicate invites.

findings.title: Existing attendees in the request receive a full new-booking confirmation
findings.description: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is given the raw input, not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts:539-547, any attendee whose email is in `newGuests` gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, the full booking confirmation. An existing attendee included in the request therefore gets that instead of the "new guests added" email. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type email-disable settings
findings.description: `sendLocationChangeEmails` takes `eventTypeMetadata` and gates the host and attendee sends with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (email-manager.ts:495-498, 503, 515). editLocation.handler.ts:135-138 passes `booking.eventType.metadata`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter, and the handler never passes metadata (addGuests.handler.ts:168). Hosts who disabled these emails still receive them. Accept the metadata and apply the same gates.

findings.title: No booking status or time check on the server
findings.description: The handler checks permissions only. It does not reject cancelled, rejected, or past bookings. The UI hides the action for cancelled and rejected bookings (BookingListItem.tsx:544-550), but it still shows the action for past confirmed bookings (lines 553-554). A direct API call against a cancelled booking adds attendees and sends invites for an event that won't happen. Check `booking.status` and `endTime` server-side.

findings.title: Any attendee can email arbitrary addresses, with no size cap or rate limit
findings.description: Anyone whose session email matches an attendee (line 52) passes the permission check. The schema has no `.max()` on the array, and the bookings router directory contains no rate-limit calls. Each call creates attendees and sends calendar invites and organizer-branded emails to arbitrary addresses. Cap guests per request and per booking, and rate-limit the mutation. The attendee grant itself is a product decision and should be confirmed.

findings.title: Permission error uses a translation key that doesn't exist
findings.description: `"you_do_not_have_permission"` is not in apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json, and it appears nowhere else in the repo. The dialog renders `t(err.message)` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43), so users see the raw key in the error toast. Add the key or reuse an existing one.

findings.title: Raw translation key used as the email HTML title
findings.description: Both templates pass `subject="guests_added_event_type_subject"`. BaseScheduledEmail computes the interpolated `subject` at line 43, but line 55 renders `props.subject || subject`, so the raw key wins. BaseEmailHtml then uses it for `<EmailHead title={props.subject} />` (BaseEmailHtml.tsx:30). The `<title>` shows `guests_added_event_type_subject`. The sent subject line is built correctly in the `.ts` classes. The fix belongs in BaseScheduledEmail.tsx:55, which should use the computed `subject`. Changing that affects other templates, so check them.

findings.title: Organizer add-guests email ignores EMAIL_FROM_NAME
findings.description: `from` uses `APP_NAME`. The base OrganizerScheduledEmail uses `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` (organizer-scheduled-email.ts:47), which is `process.env.EMAIL_FROM_NAME || APP_NAME` (packages/lib/constants.ts:31). Deployments that set `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` will see different sender names on this email. Import and use `EMAIL_FROM_NAME`.

findings.title: Dialog error state is stale, and the error fallback can never show
findings.description: `isInvalidEmail` is set true at line 56 and reset only by Cancel (line 91). On success (lines 36-41) the emails clear but the error doesn't, so the next open shows a stale "Emails must be unique and valid". Closing via `onOpenChange` (line 61) resets nothing. In `onError`, the template literal at line 43 always yields a non-empty string, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback at line 44 is unreachable. Reset the flag on success and on close, and build the fallback before the template.

findings.title: MultiEmail duplicates the existing form-builder implementation
findings.description: The new UI component is a near-copy of the inline `multiemail` factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:234-279. That factory still carries `//TODO: Make it a ui component` (line 233). The two now diverge: the form-builder version mutates `value` in place (lines 255-256), and the new one copies it. Have the form-builder factory use `@calcom/ui`'s MultiEmail and delete the copy.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip in a localized component
findings.description: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is hardcoded, while the same component localizes "Add another" through `t()`. Localized UIs will show English here. Add a locale key and use `t()`.

findings.title: No tests for the new endpoint, handler branches, or dialog
findings.description: The diff adds no test files. Nothing covers the four authorization outcomes (owner, admin, attendee, forbidden), the blacklist and dedupe logic, email classification, or the dialog validation. The bookings router directory has no tests either, so this is a gap rather than a regression. The authorization code is critical enough to be written test-first. An admin-role test would have caught the first FAIL finding.

findings.title: Lazy-load wrapper has an inaccurate copy-pasted comment
findings.description: The comment says "These are like 40kb", copied from AddressInputLazy. MultiEmail is small. The wrapper matches the existing `*Lazy` pattern, but it renders nothing until the chunk loads. The comment should be corrected, and the lazy wrapper may not be worth its cost here.

findings.title: Booking query loads organizer credentials that the handler never uses
findings.description: `credentials: true` loads every credential row, including encrypted keys, on each call. Only `destinationCalendar` is read from `booking.user`. `getUsersCredentials` (line 158) loads them separately. Drop the include.

findings.title: Calendar-event builder is copied from editLocation
findings.description: The organizer lookup, attendee mapping, and `CalendarEvent` construction match editLocation.handler.ts:31-95 almost line for line. The pattern already exists across handlers, so this is not a regression. A shared builder would stop the copies drifting.

findings.title: Router registration follows the existing handler-cache pattern
findings.description: `addGuests` uses the same `UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE` lazy import as its siblings, and the Zod input schema is attached to the procedure.

findings.title: Email template names resolve through the renderer
findings.description: `renderEmail` takes its keys from `import * as templates` (packages/emails/src/renderEmail.ts:1), and both `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` and `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` are exported from this index, so the `renderEmail(...)` calls in the `.ts` templates resolve. The i18n keys used by the email and dialog code exist in en/common.json, apart from `you_do_not_have_permission` (finding above).
